title: Start Small
description:
First real money in.

Small amount. 'Lose-and-learn money,' like Sangchul had said.

The chart turned red.

'Start small. Losing is how the market comes into focus.'
The voice came back.

choices.result_text:
Held for three days. It recovered — barely into the green.

The profit was nothing. The lesson was everything: how it rises, how it falls, how the hand trembles.
That's what Sangchul meant.

choices.text: Got greedy — added more, lost more
choices.result_text:
'Small' was heard but the hands didn't listen.

Lost it. Tuition paid the expensive way.
Real school always does.

title: Why You Started
description:
A hard stretch. Late at night.

Sangchul called. Opened with small talk, then:

'When you first came here, you said you wanted to show your father what you could do. Do you still remember what that meant to you?'

choices.text: "Yes. That reason is still with me."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul was quiet, then said:
'Then you've got it. People who know their reason don't quit when they're tired.'

After hanging up, {name} sat with the phone for a while.
This man still had a reason to check in. That was still worth something.

Sangchul waited, then said:
'That's honest. The ones who say they're sure when they aren't — those are the dangerous ones.'

'Take your time. Don't lose what you said at the beginning.'

Neither hot nor cold. It just landed.

title: Salty Again
description:
Dae-un came over again.

Opened the fridge, said 'no eggs,' went out — came back with tofu.

'Where are the eggs?'
'you don't know. The tofu just ended up in your hand.' She laughed.

This had become the routine. Wrong ingredients and all.

choices.text: Cook together tonight — that's enough for today
choices.result_text:
Salty again. Dae-un blamed {name}. {name} blamed Dae-un.
Both were lying. Both laughed.

The 3 billion won could wait until tomorrow.

The screen lit up the room. Dae-un's breathing was steady.

{name} looked at charts, numbers, tomorrow's plan.
Whether keeping her in this room was fair — unknown. Went on anyway.

title: "I Hope You Do Well"
description:
Weeks after the breakup.

Passed the pojangmacha today.

Her last words at that table came back.
'I hope you do well. Really.'

Knowing it was genuine made it stay longer.

choices.text: Use that as fuel — do well, as she said
choices.result_text:
It would be easy to resent it. Easy to dwell.

But if she meant it — then doing well was the right response.
Something like paying it back.

choices.text: Still can't walk past that pojangmacha easily
choices.result_text:
Took a different route.

Weakness or still being human — either way.
This distance will become familiar eventually. Just not yet.

title: "I Can Change"
description:
'I can change right now.'

Said it that night. It comes back sometimes.

Her answer stays longer:
'You changing isn't the problem. You chose to wait — and waiting wore you out.'

There was nothing to counter.

choices.text: That was true — and I'm actually changing
choices.result_text:
Said it to keep someone. But it stuck.

Now, when no one's watching, {name} is living it differently.
That's the residue of those words.

choices.text: Honestly — not that much has changed
choices.result_text:
True. People don't shift that fast.

At least now {name} knows the difference between meaning it and performing it.
That's accurate. It's not comfort. But it's accurate.

title: She's Doing Fine
description:
Convenience store. Part-timer mentioned something offhand.

'You know Dae-un? She used to work here. Said she's at a café now.'

{name} paused.

'Yeah. I know her.'

'She's doing well, apparently.'

choices.result_text:
Didn't do it right then.

But knowing she's doing well — something loosened.
'How are you?' had been the last thing said. Now it was almost true.

choices.text: Just say 'glad to hear it' and pay
choices.result_text:
Paid and left.

Glad to hear it. Genuinely.
The connection had ended with 'take care' — at least it was honest now.
